cards.q_text: III Code (IMO Instruments Implementation Code) — what does it say?
cards.missing_limb: Add who actually performs an IMSAS audit and where India stands: the audit is conducted by auditors nominated by other Member States and coordinated through the IMO Secretariat on a fixed cycle, and India's own audit position under that cycle.
cards.limb_sentence: The current answer lacks who actually performs an IMSAS audit - that the auditors are nominated by Member States rather than IMO staff, with the Secretariat coordinating - and where India and the audit cycle now stand.
changed_sections: answer body: new h5 'Who Actually Carries Out an IMSAS Audit' + lead paragraph + 4-item list + cycle/currentness paragraph
authority: IMO Instruments Implementation Code (III Code), resolution A.1070(28) - the audit standard applied by IMSAS.

IMO Member State Audit Scheme - audit teams are drawn from qualified auditors nominated by Member States, not IMO staff; audit officers of the IMO Secretariat coordinate the programme and support teams where necessary; mandatory since 2016 on a seven-year cycle.

IMO, 'IMO completes first global audit cycle of its Member States' - first mandatory cycle concluded 2026 with 168 Member States audited, about 94% of the membership; second cycle begins July 2027 under the revised Framework and Procedures for IMSAS adopted as resolution A.1211(34), moving to risk-based continuous monitoring.
Directorate General of Shipping / Government of India - the Indian maritime administration completed its IMSAS audit on 4 March 2024, audited as flag, port and coastal State.
required_qualifiers: does not begin to operate until the second cycle opens
forbidden_claims: audit is conducted by IMO staff
continuous monitoring mechanism is already in force
second cycle is already under way

currentness.instrument: IMO Member State Audit Scheme (IMSAS); III Code, resolution A.1070(28); revised IMSAS Framework and Procedures, resolution A.1211(34)
currentness.latest_amendment: Revised Framework and Procedures for IMSAS, resolution A.1211(34) (34th Assembly, December 2025)
currentness.mandatory_now: IMSAS mandatory since 2016; seven-year cycle; first mandatory cycle concluded 2026 (168 Member States)
currentness.adopted_not_in_force: A.1211(34) is ADOPTED; the risk-based continuous monitoring approach it introduces does NOT begin operating until the second cycle opens in July 2027. The card states this as forthcoming, not as the current regime.
currentness.card_was_stale: Not stale - SILENT. The card gave the seven-year interval and asserted in a deep-dive that "the IMO itself conducts these audits"; it never said who the auditors are, nor where India or the cycle stands.

changed_sections: answer body: new h4 'The instrument ladder - what actually binds' + lead paragraph + 6-item list + closing test paragraph
authority: TECHNICAL_REASONING_ONLY as to the taxonomy itself. The binding distinctions stated are drawn from the instruments named: MARPOL Annexes I and II compulsory for Parties with Annexes III to VI optional; codes made mandatory by reference from convention chapters (ISM via SOLAS chapter IX, ISPS via chapter XI-2, LSA via chapter III, FSS via chapter II-2, IMDG via chapter VII). No regulation number is asserted for any code-reference beyond chapter level.
required_qualifiers: no binding force of its own

authority: FAL Convention Standard 2.1 as amended by resolution FAL.14(46) (adopted 13 May 2022, in force 1 January 2024) - the declarations public authorities may require on arrival and departure, listed (a) to (m); Standard 2.1bis caps items (a) to (g) at the information in appendix 1.

authority: Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 (Act 24 of 2025), Part VII - prevention and containment of pollution from vessels and response. The enabling section block is established from the Government of India's own 2026 draft rules, each made 'in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 133(2), 133(4), 133(5), 134(1), 134(2), 135(2), 136, [140,] 142(1), 143(1) and 143(2)(n) under Part VII of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 (24 of 2025)' - Prevention of Pollution by Oil from Ships Rules 2026, Prevention of Air Pollution from Ships Rules 2026, and Prevention of Pollution by Sewage from Ships Rules 2026 (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways).

Indian Coast Guard, 'Report A Spill' (official reporting obligations): masters shall report without delay and to the fullest extent possible to the nearest Indian Coast Guard Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) the particulars of any event involving a discharge or probable discharge of oil, of any quantity, in Indian waters, and likewise for any such event observed at sea; reporting is made on the Coast Guard's Spill Notification Pro forma for Oil and HNS.
